unit.why: A single narrative about a tzaddik's last days. It runs from the fox parable on Sukkot, through his withdrawal from leadership, his anger on Shabbat after seeing the Satan, and the deaths of a maidservant and then his mother, to his words at her funeral and eulogy.
unit.boundary_note: Previous division ends a separate saying; next division (צא) continues the account of the mother's mourning and related traditions.

stories.start_quote: והנה בסיבות האחרון של ימי חייו
stories.summary_en: In his last period the tzaddik tells the fox parable in the sukkah and withdraws from being rebbe. Angry on Shabbat, he had seen the Satan enter his house, but he took the maidservant's death as the fulfilment of that sign. Heaven had misled him: his mother then died, and he invoked the tzaddikim of Ruzhin and Belz at her funeral and praised her in his eulogy.
